Preclinical models of osimertinib-resistant EGFR mutants were treated with erlotinib or afatinib. Treatment with erlotinib suppressed phosphorylation of EGFR L858R+C797S but did not decrease phosphorylation in the EGFR L858R+L718V mutant to the same extent as the EGFR L858R cell line. Mice with EGFR L858R osimertinib-resistant tumours were treated with erlotinib or afatinib. Of 16 osimertinib-resistant tumours that were also resistant to erlotinib, 3 had the L718V mutation. These tumours showed a brief transient response to erlotinib before becoming resistant.

A genetically engineered mouse model of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) was created expressing human EGFR L858R+T790M transgene. Twenty of 49 mice treated with osimertinib developed treatment-resistant tumours at an average of 8 months. Of 27 tumours examined, one contained C797G. The C797G mutation was never seen in the EGFR L858R background that lacked T790M, suggesting this resistance mutation arises more frequently in the presence of T790M.

A genetically engineered mouse model of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) was created expressing human EGFR L858R+T790M transgene. Twenty of 49 mice treated with osimertinib developed treatment-resistant tumours at an average of 8 months. Of 27 tumours examined, one contained L792H. The L792H mutation was never seen in the EGFR L858R background that lacked T790M, suggesting this resistance mutation arises more frequently in the presence of T790M.

A genetically engineered mouse model of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) was created expressing human EGFR L858R transgene. A set of osimertinib resistant tumours were treated with 25mg/kg osimertinib and 25mg/kg erlotinib to see if this combination could overcome resistance. Of 16 tumours treated, 8 responded, 2 had stable disease, and 6 progressed. Seven of 8 sensitive tumours had the C797S mutation. In addition, growth rates were assessed before and after combination treatment and C797S tumours showed negative growth rates.

A genetically engineered mouse model of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) was created expressing human EGFR L858R transgene. A set of osimertinib resistant tumours were treated with 25mg/kg osimertinib and 25mg/kg erlotinib to see if this combination could overcome resistance. Of 16 tumours treated, 8 responded, 2 had stable disease, and 6 progressed. Both tumours with stable disease and one tumour that responded had the L718Q mutation. In addition, growth rates were assessed before and after combination treatment and L718Q mutant tumours showed negative growth rates.

Patient-derived GBM brain tumour stem cells (BTSCs) were used to test the efficacy of EGFR inhibitors in vitro. Afatinib inhibited the growth and sphere-forming ability of BTSCs but not normal astrocytes. Two EGFR G598V mutant BTSC lines showed higher sensitivity to afatinib (78.9 and 0.186 nM) than most EGFR wt BTSCs (21.1-746 nM) in cell viability assays. Similar results were seen with erlotinib (3.2 and 0.14 nM) and AZD9291 (0.92 and 0.076 nM), compared to EGFR wt BTSCs (erlotinib: 0.29-17.8 nM; AZD9291: 0.193-3.4 nM).

Patient-derived GBM brain tumour stem cells (BTSCs) were used to test the efficacy of the EGFR inhibitor AZD9291 and JAK2 inhibitor pacritinib in vitro. Combination treatment with AZD9291 and pacritinib resulted in significantly decreased cell viability in EGFR G598V mutant BTSCs compared to single agent treatments, suggesting synergistic inhibition with these two drugs.

In a retrospective study of 2316 Chinese patients with stage IV non-small cell lung carcinoma, a 63 year old female with the EGFR exon 20 insertion A767_V769dupASV received osimertinib as first-line treatment. The patient achieved a partial response with greater than 30% reduction in tumour size, and progression-free survival of 6.0 months.

In a retrospective study of 2316 Chinese patients with stage IV non-small cell lung carcinoma, a 69 year old male with the novel EGFR exon 20 insertion N771_P772insL received osimertinib as first-line treatment. The patient achieved stable disease as best response with greater than 10% reduction in tumour size, and progression-free survival of 4.9 months.

A retrospective study showed that out of 11 patients with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma treated with erlotinib who carried in-frame exon 20 insertion variant, only 3 patients showed objective response rate. The median time to progression was 2.5 months.

In a retrospective study of 2316 Chinese patients with stage IV non-small cell lung carcinoma, a 63 year old female with the EGFR exon 20 insertion D770_N771insG received osimertinib as second-line treatment. The patient had clinical improvement and achieved partial response with nearly 50% reduction in tumour size. Progression-free survival was 6.4 months.

In a retrospective study of 2316 Chinese patients with stage IV non-small cell lung carcinoma, two patients with the EGFR exon 20 insertion S768_D770dup received osimertinib treatment. A 59 year old female with previous systemic treatment had a partial response and progression-free survival (PFS) of 14.6+ months, remaining on osimertinib at data cut-off. The second patient, a 70 year old female, had previous systemic therapy and treatment with the EGFR inhibitor afatinib. This patient also remained on treatment at data cut-off with stable disease and PFS of 11.2+ months.

In a retrospective study of 2316 Chinese patients with stage IV non-small cell lung carcinoma, a 65 year old female with the EGFR exon 20 insertion A763_Y764insFQEA received osimertinib as second-line treatment. The patient achieved a partial response with greater than 50% reduction in tumour size, and progression-free survival of 5.1 months. The patient had previously achieved partial response on gefinitib, but experienced disease progression after 9.0 months at which point a rebiopsy was found to harbor a T790M mutation.

A patient was initially diagnosed with stage IIIA lung adenocarcinoma with EGFR L858R and was treated with lobectomy and adjuvant pemetrexed and cisplatin. 20 months later the patient had recurrent disease in the liver, lung, and bone, and the patient was started on icotinib and a partial response was observed. After icotinib treatment a VOPP1::EGFR fusion consisting of VOPP1 exons 3-5 and EGFR exon 28, along with EGFR T790M, were detected in pericardial effusion and blood samples. The EGFR Fusion break point was between exon 27 and exon 28. Patient progressed after 6 months on icotinib and was then switched to osimertinib and experienced more than 11 months of PFS. Given that the fusion and T790M were not present until after icotinib treatment; the authors suggest that the fusion is also a resistance mechanism along with the well-known T790M resistance mutation.

Case report of a 30-year-old male with lung adenocarcinoma and metastasis to several organs, including several lesions in the brain. NGS assay (Foundation One CDX panel) detected the EGRF::RAD51 fusion. He was treated with platinum-based agents and palliative radiation therapy to the spine. Once the disease was stable as per RECIST guidelines, treatment was switched to Osimertinib. Marked improvement was seen within two weeks with reduction in lymph node metastases and reduction in back pain. Dramatic reductions in brain lesions were observed after 2 months of treatment. The patient was followed up for 9 months during which significant improvement was seen in his clinical status, and he remained on therapy at the time of publication. The authors have also noted that osimertinib fared better in improving his CNS symptoms compared to his earlier chemotherapy treatment.

items.profile: BRAF V600E AND EGFR L858R AND EGFR T790M
items.statement: A 42 year old man with non-smoking history presented with EGFR L858R positive lung adenocarcinoma. He was given various treatments including erlotinib and gefitinib and progressed four years later. biopsy revealed EGFR T790M mutation, and osimertinib treatment was given. Partial response was seen, and progression occurred after 13 months. BRAF V600E mutation was found in progressed tumor cells, but was not reported before osimertinib resistance.

items.profile: EGFR L858R OR EGFR Exon 19 Deletion
items.statement: In this phase 3, double-blind trial, 682 patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to either osimertinib (80 mg once daily) or placebo for 3 years following complete resection of EGFR mutation positive (exon 19 deletion or L858R) non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). At two years, 90% of the patients with stage II to IIIA disease in the osimertinib group (95% CI, 84 to 93) and 44% of those in the placebo group (95% CI, 37 to 51) were alive and disease-free (HR for disease recurrence or death, 0.17; 99.06% CI, 0.11 to 0.26; P < 0.001). Including all patients, 89% in the osimertinib group (95% CI, 85 to 92) and 52% of those in the placebo group (95% CI, 46 to 58) were alive and disease-free at two years (HR for disease recurrence or death, 0.20; 99.12% CI, 0.14 to 0.30; P < 0.001). In total, 29 patients died (9 in the osimertinib group and 20 in the placebo group), and grade 3 adverse events occurred in 20% of the osimertinib group versus 13% of the placebo group while 16% of the osimertinib group experienced serious adverse events versus 12% in the placebo group.

In this phase 1, open-label, dose-escalation trial, 81 patients with NSCLC involving an EGFR exon 20 insertion in phase 2 of the study were administered 1,050 mg amivantamab (1,400 mg if > 80 kg) given once weekly for the first month and then once every two weeks starting at week five based of phase 1 of the trial determining the recommended dose. The overall response rate was 40% (95% CI: 29 - 51), including three complete responses. The median duration of response of 11.1 months (95% CI: 6.9 - not reached) and the median progression-free survival was 8.3 months (95% CI: 6.5 - 10.9).

In this open-label phase1/2 trial, 114 patients with EGFR exon 20 insertion NSCLC who were previously treated with platinum received 160 mg mobocertinib once daily. The primary endpoint was confirmed objective response rate (ORR). The median follow-up period was 14.2 months, with a confirmed ORR of 28% (95% CI: 20% - 37%) by independent review committee (IRC) assessment and 35% (95% CI: 26% - 45%) by investigator assessment. The median duration of response was 17.5 months (95% CI: 7.4 - 20.3) by IRC assessment. Further, the median progression-free survival was 7.3 months (95% CI: 5.5 - 9.2) by IRC assessment. Lastly, the median overall survival was 24.0 months (95% CI: 14.6 - 28.8). 19 of 114 patients discontinued treatment because of adverse effects, dose reductions due to an adverse effect occurred in 29 of 114 patients, and response rates were greater in the 85 patients without dose reduction.

items.profile: EGFR S768I OR EGFR G719A OR EGFR L861Q
items.statement: In a phase 2 trial, 129 patients with lung adenocarcinoma with EGFR mutations including mutations other than exon 19 deletions or exon 21 L858R substitutions who had no more than one previous chemotherapy regimen for advanced disease or an EGFR tyrosine-kinase inhibitor. 99 patients started with a dose of 50 mg and the other 30 patients with a starting dose of 40 mg. 79 of 129 patients had an objective response (two complete responses, 77 partial responses). 70 of the 106 patients with exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R EGFR mutations had an objective response, as did nine of 23 patients with the less common mutations. Median progression-free survival was 10.1 months (95% CI: 8.12 – 13.80, however, median progression-free survival was shorter for patients with the uncommon mutations. The median overall survival was 24.8 months (95% CI: 21.98 – 38.74), and the median overall survival for patients with the less common mutations was again shorter. Grade 3 adverse events were more common in patients receiving the higher 50 mg starting dose, and there was one possible drug-related death secondary to interstitial lung disease.

items.profile: EGFR L858R OR EGFR Exon 19 Deletion
items.statement: In this phase 3, open-label, randomized trial, 452 patients with EGFR mutation-positive non-small cell lung cancer including exon 19 deletions and exon 21 L858R point mutations were randomized into cohorts receive either oral dacomitinib 45 mg/day or oral gefitinib 250 mg/day, both in 28-day cycles. The median duration for follow-up for progression-free survival was 22.1 months (95% CI: 20.3 – 23.9), and the median progression-free was 14.7 months (95% CI: 11.1 – 16.6) in the dacomitinib cohort versus 9.2 months (9.1 – 11.0) in the gefitinib group (hazard ratio: 0·59, 95% CI: 0·47 – 0·74; p < 0.0001). Treatment-related serious adverse events were observed in 21 patients given dacomitinib and in ten patients given gefitinib. Further, two treatment-related deaths occurred in the dacomitinib group and one in the gefitinib.

items.profile: EGFR L858R OR EGFR Exon 19 Deletion
items.statement: In this phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 449 patients stage IV NSCLC with EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 (L858R) mutations. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive oral erlotinib (150 mg/day) plus either intravenous ramucirumab (10 mg/kg) or matching placebo once every 2 weeks. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival. The median duration of follow-up was 20.7 months (IQR: 15.8–27.2), and the progression-free survival was found to be significantly longer in the ramucirumab plus erlotinib group 19.4 months (95% CI: 15.4 – 21.6) than in the placebo plus erlotinib group at 12.4 months (11.0 – 13.5), with a hazard ratio of 0.59 (95% CI: 0.46 – 0·76; p < 0·0001). Lastly, grade 3/4 adverse events were reported in 159 of 221 patients in the ramucirumab plus erlotinib group versus 121 of 225 in the placebo plus erlotinib group, and one death was recorded in the ramucirumab plus erlotinib group.

items.profile: EGFR L858R OR EGFR Exon 19 Deletion
items.statement: In this phase-IV, open-label, single-arm study, 106 patients with NSCLC and EGFR mutations including exon 19 deletion and exon 21 L858R point mutations were administered 250 mg daily doses of gefitinib with the primary endpoint being objective response rate (ORR). The objective response rate was 69.8% (95% CI: 60.5 – 77.7), with a median progression-free survival of 9.7 months (95% CI: 8.5 – 11.0), and a median overall survival of 19.2 months (95% CI:17.0 – not calculable).

In this phase 2 study, 129 patients with NSCLC, including those with less common, non-resistant EGFR mutations such as S768I, L861Q, and/or G719X, were treated with afatinib in two cohorts: 99 with a starting dose of 50 mg and 30 with a starting dose of 40 mg. 79 of 129 patients had an objective response (two complete responses, 77 partial responses), and included in that is nine of the 23 patients harbouring the less common mutations. Similar proportions of patients had an objective response when the starting dose was accounted for (18/30 patients at 40 mg versus 61/99 patients at 50 mg). Both progression-free survival and overall survival was higher for the common mutation group versus the less common mutations.

In this study, 4 patients with an EGFR exon 19 insertion and 6 patients with an EGFR exon 20 insertion (A763_Y764insFQEA) were enrolled. Hospital. Among patients with an exon 19 insertion, 3 received an EGFR TKI. Of the 3 patients, 1 had a partial response, 1 had stable disease, and 1 had progressive disease. Of the 6 patients with the exon 20 insertion (A763_Y764insFQEA), 3 received an EGFR TKI. Of those 3 patients, 2 had a partial response and 1 had progressive. Two patients with exon 20 insertion (A763_Y764insFQEA) received erlotinib, resulting in a partial response in one patient and progressive disease in the other, with progression-free survival rates of 14.5 and three months, respectively.

items.profile: EGFR Exon 19 Deletion AND MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation
items.statement: A 53-year old woman (former smoker: 15 pack-years) was diagnosed with non-small-cell lung cancer that revealed an adenocarcinoma. Initial tumor was sequenced to find an EGFR exon 19 deletion mutation and was subsequently treated with 3 cycles of cisplatin and pemetrexed. After partial remission, ablative radio-chemotherapy was performed at 50.4 Gy on tumor site and 61.6 Gy on metastases. After 12-month progression-free survival, the patient developed new metastases and was revealed to have a MET exon 14 skipping mutation via next-generation sequencing. Afatinib was given at 40 mg daily, but progression was seen after 6 weeks. 250 mg of crizotinib twice daily was added to afatinib treatment (reduced to 30 mg) and was well-tolerated. There was a tremendous response with complete remission of liver metastases and partial remission of pulmonary tumor manifestations after 6 weeks.

A 73-year old male (non-smoker) with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) was found to have EGFR L858R mutation and MET amplification. The patient had a dramatic response to erlotinib and crizotinib but after 10 months, the disease progressed. Next-generation sequencing showed EGFR L858R mutation again, but increased MET amplification (MET-to-centromere of chromosome 7 ratio > 25). The patient received preliminary systemic chemotherapy but after 7 months, disease progressed with CNS symptoms in line with enhancing brain lesions. 250 mg gefitinib was administered daily in combination with 400 mg of capmatinib twice daily. Scans after 6 weeks of treatment showed intracranial response with well tolerated treatment. Capmatinib needed to be reduced to 300 mg twice daily due to grade 3 transaminase elevations. The authors report the patient has received treatment for 19 months ongoing with no evidence of systemic disease.

items.profile: EGFR Exon 19 Deletion AND MET Y1003N
items.statement: A 65-year old female diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma revealed several brain lesions, the largest measuring 1.8 x 1.5 x 1.9 cm. COBAS EGFR mutation test was run and revealed EGFR exon 19 deletion mutation. Patient was started on osimertinib 80 mg once daily and achieved partial response, showing a shrinkage of smaller brain lesions and left lower lung mass. 19 months into treatment, brain MRI scans showed an increase in size of lesions, consistent with an increase in symptoms. Following 3 cycles of increased osimertinib dosage in combination with carboplatin and pemetrexed, the patient's condition worsened and showed increased size and density of lung cancer. Next-generation sequencing revealed MET Y1003N mutation. 300 mg capmatinib twice a day was given in combination with osimertinib 80 mg daily, which both were slowly moved up to 400 mg and 160 mg respectively. Response was observed in the chest with shrinkage of right-sided lung lesions. The authors suggest osimertinib and capmatinib has a potential role in progressive EGFR-mutated NSCLC with resistant MET mutations.

items.profile: EGFR Mutation AND ( MET Amplification OR MET Overexpression )
items.statement: This phase 1b/2, multicentre, randomized clinical trial was conducted on the combination of tepotinib and gefitinib on patients with MET overexpression or MET amplification that showed resistance to EGFR TKI therapies. For phase 1b, the median duration of tepotinib and gefitinib therapy was 18.5 weeks at 300 mg and 16.9 mg at 500 mg, with no dose-limiting toxic effects at either dosage. Thus, it was established that tepotinib in combination with gefitinib should be 500 mg once daily. In the phase 2 study, the authors report that progression-free survival and overall survival was improved by tepotinib with gefitinib in patients with MET overexpression and MET amplification. Patients with MET IHC3+ (overexpression) had a median overall survival of 37.3 months (24.2 - 37.3) with the treatment vs with traditional chemotherapy of 17.9 months (12.0 - 20.7). In MET amplification, with tepotinib and gefitinib, overall survival was 37.3 months (NE - NE) vs chemotherapy 13.1 months (3.25 - NE).

items.profile: EGFR G719A AND MET Splice Site (c.2888-21_2888-20delinsGC)
items.statement: A 60-year old man (smoker: 300 pack-years) presented with lung adenocarcinoma measuring 3.0 x 2.3 cm and multiple lymph node metastases. Next-generation sequencing revealed a EGFR G719A (abundance 5.08%) and MET exon 14 skipping mutation (c.2888-21_2888-20delinsGC) (abundance 8.61%). The patient was given 30 mg of afatinib daily and 250 mg of crizotinib twice daily and partial response was seen after 6 weeks. The authors report that the patient has obtained the continued response for 3 months.

items.profile: EGFR T790M AND EGFR Exon 19 Deletion
items.statement: This phase 3 trial (NCT02151981) involved 419 patients with EGFR T790M mutant NSCLC who progressed after first-line EGFR inhibitor therapy (gefitinib, erlotinib, or afatinib) and were either treated with the third-generation EGFR inhibitor osimertinib or platinum therapy plus pemetrexed.  The objective response rate was 71% (95% CI: 65 to 76) with osimertinib compared to 31% (95% CI: 24 to 40) with platinum/pemetrexed. The median progression free survival (PFS) for osimertinib was 10.1 months compared to 4.4 months with platinum/pemetrexed. In patients with CNS metastases, osimertinib demonstrated a longer median duration of PFS (8.5 months vs. 4.2 months) as well.  Of note, the osimertinib-treated EGFR T790M patients had other co-occuring EGFR mutations including 68% with exon 19 deletions, 30% with L858R, 1% with a G719X mutation, and 1 patient each with S768I and an exon 20 insertion.  Osimertinib treatment of patients with exon 19 deletion plus T790M resulted in a hazard ration of 0.34  (95% CI: 0.24-0.46) and L858R plus T790M resulted in a hazard ratio of 0.46 (95% CI: 0.30-0.71).  The study concludes that osimertinib exhibited significantly greater efficacy in patients with EGFR T790M mutant advanced NSCLC, even in those with CNS metastases, whose disease had progressed during first-line EGFR inhibitor therapy, independent of co-occuring EGFR mutation.

The drug sensitivity of 55 non-synonymous ERBB2 missense variants were assessed using the mixed-all-nominated-in-one (MANO) method, both in vitro (introduced into Ba/F3 cells; experiment conducted in triplicate) and in vivo (tumor xenograft model). ERBB2-targeted inhibitors included in this study include trasztuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib and osimertinib. Drug sensitivity was reported as sensitive, partially sensitive and resistant, as determined by the IC50 of each drug against each missense variant. Sensitivity of this variant to the listed therapies: sensitive.

items.profile: EGFR T790M AND EGFR Exon 19 Deletion AND MET Splice Site (c.3027_3028+21delAGGTATATTTCAGTTTATTGTTC
items.statement: A 53-year old man (non-smoker) presented with chest tightness and pain and was revealed to have stage IV lung adenocarcinoma with EGFR exon 19 deletion. The patient started first-line Erlotinib at 150 mg daily dose with partial response. After 28 months, new bone metastases formed and it was revealed to have developed a EGFR T790M mutation along with EGFR exon 19 deletion. Treatment was modified to Osimertinib at 80 mg daily which led to partial response for 15.4 months until progression of new bone metastases. Next-generation sequencing revealed a MET exon 14 skipping mutation (c.3027_3028+21delAGGTATATTTCAGTTTATTGTTC) and MET fusion (EX13:EX15) combined with the original EGFR exon 19 deletion. Combination therapy was started with Osimertinib (80 mg daily) + Capamatinib (400 mg, twice daily). This yielded parietal response and progression-free survival for 7 months. Upon examinations, there was disappearance of MET exon 14 skipping mutation and improvement of symptoms. There was also maintenance of bone metastasis as well.

In this phase 3 trial, 308 patients with NSCLC harbouring EGFR exon 20 insertions were treated with a combination of amivantamab and chemotherapy (carboplatin-pemetrexed) [n = 153] or chemotherapy alone [n = 155]. The median PFS in the aminvantamab-chemotherapy group was 11.4 months which was significantly higher than the chemotherapy group (median PFS of 6.7 months). The hazard ratio reported for disease progression was 0.40 (95% CI, 0.30 - 0.53, p <0.001), while the hazard ratio reported for death for amivantamab-chemotherapy compared to chemotherapy was 0.67 (95% CI; 0.42 - 1.09, p =0.11). The median objective response in the amivantamab-chemotherapy group was 9.7 months (95% CI; 8.2-13.5) compared to 4.4 months (95% CI; 4.1-5.6) in the chemotherapy group. The majority of patients in the cohort reported at least one adverse event. Overall, the study reported significantly better clinical results in the patients treated with amivantamab-chemotherapy combination therapy compared to patients treated with chemotherapy alone as a first-line treatment.

items.profile: EGFR L858R OR EGFR Exon 19 Deletion
items.statement: In this phase 3 clinical trial, 557 patients with NSCLC harbouring EGFR mutations (exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation) were randomly assigned to two groups and treated with either osimertinib with chemotherapy or osimertinib monotherapy. Significantly higher PFS was noted in the group treated with osimertinib and chemotherapy compared to osimertinib monotherapy, with a hazard ratio of 0.62 (95% CI; 0.49 - 0.79, p < 0.0001). After 24 months, 57% (95% CI; 50-63) and 41% (95% CI; 35-47) of the patients in the osimertinib and chemotherapy versus osimertinib monotherapy groups respectively, were alive and progression-free. An objective response was reported in 83% of the patients in the osimertinib-chemotherapy group, while an objective response was observed in 76% of the patients in the osimertinib monotherapy group. Grade ≥ 3 AEs were observed more frequently in the combination therapy group compared to the monotherapy group.

items.profile: ERBB2 Activating Mutation OR ERBB2 T790M
items.statement: In this phase 2 clinical trial, 19 patients with tumours harbouring EGFR mutations (T790M or activation mutations) were treated with osimertinib, an EGFR TKI. Of the 19 patients, 13 were evaluable for efficacy. The ORR and 6-month PFS was 15.4% (90% CI; 2.8 - 41.0) and 16.7% (90% CI; 0-34.4) respectively. Overall, the study did not meet its prespecified end-point and therefore found no clinically relevant benefit of osimertinib treatment within their cohort.

A 57-year old male with no significant smoking history presented with lung squamous cell carcinoma in the right lung. Oncomine Dx Target Test was done and revealed EGFR exon 19 deletion and de novo EGFR T790M mutation. Patient was treated with chemotadiotherapy and one course of durvalumab until a brain metastasis appeared. Stereotactic radiotherapy was then performed, but 4 months after the termination of durvalumab, the tumor increased in size. Treatment was then switched to osimertinib and partial response was achieved two months later. The authors also summarized 16 other cases of lung squamous cell carcinoma patients that were treated with osimertinib, 12 of which responded in partial responses.

Ba/F3 mouse lymphoid cells expressing wild-type or V777L mutant HER2 were treated with afatinib, neratinib, osimertinib or DMSO (vehicle) for 72 hours, at which time viable cells were measured using the Alamar Blue cell viability assay. Comparison of IC50 values demonstrated that cells expressing V777L mutant HER2 were sensitive to all three drugs. A separate experiment assessing the relative growth of V777L HER2-transduced Ba/F3 cells in the presence of inhibitors indicated that compared to wild-type the cells expressing the mutant protein were also sensitive to lapatinib and sapatinib but resistant to trastuzumab.

Osimertinib was effective in achieving a partial response in a patient with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer metastasis in the brain harboring ERBB2 exon 19 c.2262_2264delinsTCC, p.(L755P) variant.

Using the MANO competitive proliferation assay, Ba/F3 cells expressing ERBB2 G292R were treated for 72 hours with trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, or osimertinib. Relative cell abundance was normalized to the corresponding vehicle-treated control, and ERBB2 G292R was sensitive to all six therapies.

items.profile: EGFR L858R OR EGFR Exon 19 Deletion
items.statement: In this trial (MARIPOSA), 1074 patients with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer harbouring exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R substitution were randomized (2:2:1) to receive lazertinib-amivantamab (n=429), osimertinib monotherapy (n=429) or lazertininib monotherapy (n=216). Patients who received lazertinib-amivantamab combination therapy had a significantly higher median PFS compared to patients who received osimertinib monotherapy (23.7 months vs. 16.6 months; HR 0.70 [95% CI, 0.58-0.85; p < 0.001]). Additionally, amivantamab-lazertinib prolonged PFS vs. osimertinib in patients with a history of brain metastases (18.3 months vs. 13.0 months; HR 0.69 [95% CI, 0.53-0.92]). In 136 patients with liver metastases at baseline, the median PFS was significantly prolonged in patients treated with amivantamab-lazertinib (18.2 months, 95% CI, 13.1-NE) compared to patients treated with osimertinib (11.0 months, 95% CI, 7.4-12.8), while the HR for disease progression in the amivantamab-lazertinib versus osimertinib groups was 0.58 (95% CI, 0.37-0.91, p = 0.017).

NSCLC with EGFR activating alterations are frequently treated with the tyrosine kinase inhibitor, osimertinib. Though initially very effective, cancers cells often develop resistance to osimertinib through acquisition of additional alterations that maintains the proliferation capacity. Combinatorial treatment of osimertinib and BMVC-8C3O prevented acquisition of osimertinib resistance and inhibited the growth of osimertinib-resistant tumors. Treatment with BMVC-8C3O resulted in reduction of both mRNA and protein c-FOS levels and causes the osimertinib and BMVC-8C3O synergistic cytotoxicity. The synergist effect is mainly due to simultaneous suppression of the PI3K/AKT pathway and c-FOS, however this combination did not affect ERK activity.

items.profile: EGFR L858R OR EGFR Exon 19 Deletion
items.statement: The phase 3 randomized LAURA trial (NCT NCT03521154) evaluated osimertinib as consolidation therapy after definitive chemoradiation in 216 patients with unresectable stage 3 non-small cell lung cancer harboring an EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation. Patients were allocated 2:1 to treatment with osimertinib or placebo until disease progression. The primary endpoint of progression-free survival (PFS) favored the osimertinib arm with a hazard ratio of 0.16 (95% CI, 0.10 to 0.24, P<0.001). The median PFS was 39.1 months for osimertinib vs 5.6 months for placebo. Overall survival data were not mature at the time of publication; eighty-one percent of the patients in the placebo arm received osimertinib after progression.

In this phase III trial, 657 patients with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC (Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer) harbouring EGFR mutations (exon 19 deletions or L858R) were treated with amivantamab plus carboplatin-pemetrexed (chemotherapy). These patients were then randomized 2:2:1 to receive amivantamab-lazertinib-chemotherapy (n=263), chemotherapy (n=263), or amivantamab-chemotherapy (n=131). 

PFS was significantly longer in the amivantamab-chemotherapy [median 6.3 months; HR 0.48, p <0.001] and the amivantamab-lazertinib-chemotherapy [median 8.3 months; HR 0.44, p <0.001] groups compared to chemotherapy alone [median 4.2 months]. Additionally, ORR was also significantly higher in the amivantamab-chemotherapy and amivantamab-lazertinib-chemotherapy groups at, 64% (95% CI 55-72) and 63% (95% CI 57-69) respectively, compared to the chemotherapy group alone at 36% (p < 0.001 for both).

The goal of this study was to assess the frequency, overall survival, and classifying actionability of EGFR mutations in NSCLC within the Dutch population from 2013-2017. This study found that despite an increase in the number of patients tested, still 12% of patients have EGFR mutations and the distribution of the EGFR variants remained constant. This study assessed common EGFR mutations, exon 19 deletion and L858R, as compared to non-actionable/unknown/uncommon variants. They found that overall survival improved for people with EGFR mutations from 2013 to 2017. Patients with either an exon 19 deletion or L858R variant were more likely to receive first-line treatment (either gefitinib, erlotinib, or afatinib), additionally they found that EGFR exon 19 deletions had superior outcomes compared to L858R. 8.4% of exon 19 deletion patients treated with first-line treatments developed EGFR T790M mutation as a mechanism of resistance. Further studies need to be conducted as to whether Osimertinib is more effective for patients who develop T790M resistance in an exon 19 deletion or L858R background.

Transformed Ba/F3 cells expressing p.P772_H773insDNP, also known as p.D770_P772dup, is partially sensitive (100nM =< IC90 =< 500nM) to Osimertinib using the in vitro MANO assay and PrestoBlue cell viability assay. In comparison, cells expressing p.L858R is sensitive (IC90 < 100nM) to the compound. In vivo MANO method using NIH3T3 xenograft in nude mice demonstrated this variant is partially sensitive (0% =< tumour size change % =< -80%, 20% =< ORR% =< 50%) to Osimertinib (20mg/kg body weight).

This is a case report of 29-year-old diagnosed with metastatic adenocarcinoma of the left lung. The patient was treated with chemotherapy (cisplatin 75 mg/m2 and pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 every 3 weeks) and immunotherapy (pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks) for 4 cycles then maintenance with pembrolizumab and pemetrexed for 4 cycles before PD on lungs, brain and lymph nodes. FoundationOne DX1 on a new mediastinal lymph node biopsy detected an EGFR::RAD51 fusion. Patient was then treated with erlotinib (150mg/d) and achieved PR on all tumour sites three weeks following treatment initiation. The patient was switched to Osimertinib (80 mg/d) after being on erlotinib for two months due to renal toxicity. Further tumour response was observed at subsequent restating imaging and the patient is still on treatment 10 months since EGFR-TKI initiation.

This is a case report of a 45-year-old male never smoker that was diagnosed with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma. The patient responded poorly to the initial chemoimmunotherapy (carboplatin, pemetrexed, nivolumab, and ipilimumab) and progressively deteriorated. Following the detection of an EGFR::RAD51 gene fusion by repeat NGS using FoundationOne Liquid CDx, the patient was treated with Osimertinib (80mg/d) and experienced dramatic symptom improvement within one month of treatment initiation. Despite asymptomatic intracranial metastases with stable systemic disease at 9 months, the patient remained on therapy and continued to show PR 12 months after initiation of Osimertinib.

This is a case report of a 58-year-old never-smoker diagnosed with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma. The patient was treated with multiple lines of chemotherapy ((1) carboplatin/pemetrexed, (2)docetaxel 75 mg/m2 once every 3 weeks/ramucirumab, (3)  paclitaxel/ramucirumab, and (4)gemcitabine) prior to developing peritoneal progression. An EGFR::ERBB4 fusions was then identified using Foundation Medicine. The DNA-based testing demonstrated fusion between EGFR exons 1-27 and EGFR exons 18-28, while subsequent RNA-based fusion testing demonstrated an in-frame transcript coupling EGFR exon 25 to ERBB4 exon 18. Following identification of the EGFR::ERBB4 fusion, the patient was enrolled in a trial of tarloxotinib, a pan-ERBB/HER kinase inhibitor, which was discontinued after <4 months following further peritoneal progression and ovarian metastases. The patient was then enrolled in a trial of fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki (T-DXd), where she remained on therapy with stable disease for approximately 20 months until peritoneal and ovarian progression. The patient then received mobocertinib (160mg/d), achieving CR of all peritoneal lesion and PR of ovarian metastases on the initial scan. Dozens of intraparenchymal foci were detected approximately 6 months following mobocertinib initiation, patient was switched to Osimertinib (80mg/d)  which led to continuous PR in the ovaries, resolution of brain metastases, and reduction of the lesion in the right front lobe. The patient remains on Osimertinib eight months after.

Sensitivity was assessed by YFP-EGFR-ICD relocation following treatment.

In a multinational open label phase II dose randomized study of sunvozertinib in platinum pretreated advanced NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations (WU-KONG1B, NCT03974022; efficacy n = 85 for 200 mg-random, n = 89 for 300 mg-random, and n = 107 for 300 mg-all), sunvozertinib produced IRC confirmed ORRs of 45.9% (97.5% CI, 33.6 - 58.5), 47.2% (97.5% CI, 35.1 - 59.5), and 45.8% (97.5% CI, 34.8 - 57.0) at 200 mg-random, 300 mg-random, and 300 mg-all, respectively (P < 0.0001 vs null ORR 17%), with median PFS 8.4, 7.7, and 6.9 months and 12-month OS rates 62.1, 73.7, and 69.4%. Across the 200 mg-random and 300 mg-random cohorts, the 770_SVD subtype represented 24.7% and 18.0% of patients, with cORRs of 47.6% and 56.3%, respectively. Meanwhile, the 769_ASV subtype accounted for 21.2% and 23.6%, with cORRs of 33.3% and 57.1%, respectively. 
Across treated patients (200 mg-random n = 91; 300 mg-all n = 111), grade ≥3 treatment related AEs occurred in 40.7% and 58.6%, most commonly diarrhea (2.2% vs 18.0%), blood CPK increase (6.6% vs 12.6%), and anemia (4.4% vs 6.3%), with no treatment related deaths; both dose levels met the prespecified primary endpoint of IRC confirmed ORR.

Exon20ins variants grouped as “Others” comprised 48.2% and 53.9% of patients in the 200 mg‐random and 300 mg‐random cohorts with cORRs of 46.3% and 39.6%, respectively.
Across treated patients (200 mg-random n = 91; 300 mg-all n = 111), grade ≥3 treatment related AEs occurred in 40.7% and 58.6%, most commonly diarrhea (2.2% vs 18.0%), blood CPK increase (6.6% vs 12.6%), and anemia (4.4% vs 6.3%), with no treatment related deaths; both dose levels met the prespecified primary endpoint of IRC confirmed ORR.

In a single-center retrospective review of recurrent malignant gliomas with EGFR alterations (n = 6, 2 GBM), osimertinib showed a manageable safety profile with thrombocytopenia in 2 patients (grade 2 and grade 3 on concurrent bevacizumab) and no rash or QTc prolongation. Among 4 patients evaluable for radiographic response, 1 achieved PR and 2 achieved SD with times on osimertinib of 77–294 days, including 2 EGFR vIII altered GBMs that remained on treatment for 236 and at least 294 days. These findings suggest that EGFR vIII rearrangements with amplification may be associated with extended clinical benefit on osimertinib in heavily pretreated (≥2 prior regimens) current malignant glioma.

An in vitro study transformed Ba/F3 murine cells (IL-3 dependent lymphocyte model) with one of five uncommon EGFR mutations: Del18 (delE709_T710insD), E709K, G719A, S768I, and L861Q. The response to current and novel EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI) was assessed using a growth inhibition assay. Transformed cells harbouring these mutations had the largest inhibitory effect when exposed to afatinib (a second generation TKI), with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration ranging from 0.2 to 1.7 nM. In addition, these cells also had the strongest inhibitory effect on mutant tumor cells compared to wild-type EGFR non-cancerous cells, with a selectivity index ranging from 0.29 to 2.5.

An in vitro study transformed Ba/F3 murine cells (IL-3 dependent lymphocyte model) with one of five uncommon EGFR mutations: Del18 (delE709_T710insD), E709K, G719A, S768I, and L861Q. The response to current and novel EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI) was assessed using a growth inhibition assay. Transformed cells harboring exon 18 mutations (Del18, E709K, and G719A) had a moderate to strong inhibitory effect when exposed to befotertinib (a third generation TKI), with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration of 24, 14, and 1.2 nM respectively. In addition, all the mutations exhibited a low sensitivity index ranging from 0.12-2.4; a low sensitivity index equates to a stronger inhibitory effect of mutant EGFR on tumor cells compared to wild-type EGFR on non-cancerous cells.

An in vitro study treated Ba/F3 murine cells (IL-3 dependent lymphocyte model) to afatinib, a second-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), for several weeks. Secondary resistant mutations to afatinib were examined. In cells originally transformed with the EGFR S768I mutation, those hit with a secondary T790M mutation only showed sensitivity to lazertinib (a novel third-generation TKI), with a sensitivity index of 4.6.

An in vitro study treated Ba/F3 murine cells (IL-3 dependent lymphocyte model) to afatinib, a second-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), for several weeks. Secondary resistant mutations to afatinib were examined. In cells originally transformed with the EGFR S768I mutation, those hit with a secondary T769L/M mutation were resistant to all TKIs with a sensitivity index greater than 10. These TKIs include the current standard treatments (afatinib, osimertinib), and novel third-generation TKIs (furmonertinib, lazertinib, almonertinib, rezivertinib, and befotertinib).

Two uncommon EGFR frameshift deletions (E701fs and L702fs; VAFs of 32.8% and 21.5%, respectively) were identified by NGS in a patient with NSCLC. The patient was enrolled in the OCELOT clinical trial and started first-line osimertinib 80 mg daily. Treatment was well tolerated, with significant improvement in symptoms. The patient remained active and independent, reporting good appetite and no gastrointestinal issues or new pain. Recent imaging showed decreased left perihilar and mid-lung opacity, and tumor markers CEA and CA125 improved. The latest CT scan demonstrated a partial response with residual left lung opacity of 2.2 cm per RECIST criteria.

This clinical study focuses on 105 participants included in the CHRYSALIS-2 Cohort (Cohort C), examining the treatment outcome of atypical EGFR mutation non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) to a combined treatment of amivantamab and lazertinib, excluding coexisting exon 20 insertions, exon 19 deletions, or exon 21 L858R mutations from the patient cohort. Patients had received at most 2 other lines of treatment to qualify for the trial, excluding those who had received any form of third generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs). Treated CNS metastases were permitted if patient was stable. Participants were treated with 1,050 mg intravenous amivantamab once a week for the first 4 weeks and then once every 2 weeks as well as 240 mg oral lazertinib once daily. In atypical EGFR mutation patients (n=38) a second generation EGFR-TKI, afatinib, had a median progression-free survival rate of 10.7 months (PMID: 26051236). In this study the overall median progression-free survival rate was 11.1 months (95% CI, 7.8 to 17.8), the treatment-naive subgroup (n=49) saw a median progression-free survival rate of 19.5 months (95% CI, 11.2 to Not Estimable), and previously-treated group (n=56) had a median progression-free survival rate of 7.8 months (95% CI, 5.4 to 11.1).

A 53-year-old Chinese man and lifelong non-smoker presented with chest tightness and pain. CT scans revealed multiple small lung nodules in the right lower lobe were seen with CT scan. Biopsy confirmed stage IV lung adenocarcinoma with EGFR exon 19 deletion. First-line treatment with Erlotinib at a daily dose of 150 mg resulted in a partial response and tumors regressed. After 28 months, there was primary tumor enlargement and the emergence of new bone metastases. Biopsy confirmed the presence of both EGFR exon 19 deletion and T790M mutation.

items.statement: A 53-year-old Chinese man, a lifelong non-smoker, presented with chest tightness and pain. CT imaging revealed multiple small nodules in the right lower lobe of the lung. A biopsy confirmed stage IV lung adenocarcinoma with an EGFR exon 19 deletion. First-line treatment with Erlotinib (150 mg daily) resulted in a partial response, with regression of the tumors. After 28 months, disease progression was observed, characterized by enlargement of the primary tumor and the development of new bone metastases. Repeat biopsy confirmed the persistence of the EGFR exon 19 deletion along with the acquisition of a T790M mutation. The patient was subsequently treated with second-line Osimertinib (80 mg daily), achieving another partial response that lasted 15.4 months.
